title: Homologous series
keyIdea: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and the same general formula. Neighbouring members differ by CH₂, they react in similar ways, and physical properties such as boiling point change gradually along the series.

kid: Organic compounds come in families. Chemists call each family a homologous series. Alkanes are one family. Alcohols are another.
Members of a family are like steps on a ladder. Each step adds one more CH₂: one carbon and two hydrogens. Methanol is CH₃OH. Ethanol is C₂H₅OH. Propanol is C₃H₇OH.

What makes a family is a special group of atoms called the functional group. Every alcohol has an OH group. Every alkene has a C=C bond. The group is the part that reacts, so members of a family react in a similar way.
They are not all the same, though. Bigger members boil at higher temperatures. Each step up the ladder makes the boiling point rise a bit more.
adult: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds. All its members share a functional group and one general formula. Four examples are the alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, the alkenes, CₙH₂ₙ, the alcohols, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, and the carboxylic acids.

Each member differs from the next by one CH₂ unit. Going from ethanol, C₂H₅OH, to propanol, C₃H₇OH, adds one carbon and two hydrogens, and the –OH stays. That steady step is why one formula covers the whole family.

The functional group is the atom or group of atoms that decides how a compound reacts. All alcohols burn and react with sodium because they all carry –OH. Physical properties change step by step instead: boiling point rises as the chain grows, from −162 °C for methane to 36 °C for pentane.

Common mistakes: thinking neighbours differ by CH₃; putting two compounds in one series because they have the same number of carbons, such as ethane and ethanol; and expecting members to have identical properties when only their reactions are alike.

familyTip: Find two or three products at home that list an alcohol, such as hand gel (ethanol) or some cleaners (propanol). Write their formulae on a strip of paper as a ladder: CH₃OH, C₂H₅OH, C₃H₇OH. Ask each other what is added at every step and what never changes.

worked.title: Is C₄H₉OH in the same homologous series as ethanol, C₂H₅OH? If so, how far apart are they?
steps: Check the functional group first. Both formulae end in OH, so both are alcohols.
Check the general formula. For alcohols it is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. With n = 4 that gives C₄H₉OH, so it fits.
Find the difference: C₄H₉OH − C₂H₅OH = C₂H₄, which is 2 × CH₂.
So yes, they are in the same series, two members apart: ethanol, then propanol, then butanol.

practice.prompt: Two neighbouring members of a homologous series differ by what?
practice.hint: Compare CH₄ with C₂H₆: count the extra carbons and the extra hydrogens.
practice.explain: CH₄ to C₂H₆ adds 1 C and 2 H, which is CH₂. Every neighbouring pair in a series differs by exactly this.

practice.prompt: In a homologous series, one member has {a} carbon atoms. How many CH₂ units must be added to reach the member with {b} carbon atoms?
practice.hint: Each CH₂ unit adds exactly one carbon atom. Count the extra carbons.

practice.prompt: A CH₂ unit has a relative mass of 14. Two members of the same series differ by {k} CH₂ units. How much larger is the relative formula mass of the bigger one?
practice.hint: Each CH₂ adds 12 for the carbon and 2 for the hydrogens.
practice.explain: {k} × 14 = {=14*k}, so the bigger molecule is {=14*k} heavier.

practice.prompt: Which compound is in the same homologous series as ethanol, C₂H₅OH?
practice.hint: Look for the same functional group, not the same number of carbons.
practice.explain: C₃H₇OH, propanol, has –OH and is one CH₂ bigger. C₂H₆ has no –OH, and CH₃COOH has –COOH, a different group.

practice.prompt: Which statement about the members of a homologous series is true?
choices: They react in similar ways, and their boiling points change gradually
They all have the same boiling point
They all have the same number of carbon atoms
practice.hint: Think about what the shared functional group controls, and what changes as the chain grows.
practice.explain: The shared group gives similar reactions. Boiling point rises steadily with chain length, and the carbon count changes by one each step.

pool.prompt: What decides which homologous series a compound belongs to?
pool.hint: Which part of the molecule decides how it reacts?
pool.explain: The functional group, such as –OH or C=C, defines the family. Compounds with the same number of carbons can be in different series.

pool.prompt: Propene, C₃H₆, is an alkene. What is the next alkene in the series?
pool.hint: Add one CH₂ to C₃H₆: one more C and two more H.
pool.explain: C₃H₆ + CH₂ = C₄H₈, butene. C₄H₁₀ has no C=C, so it is an alkane.

pool.prompt: Butane boils at −1 °C and hexane at 69 °C. Which is the best estimate for pentane, the alkane between them?
pool.hint: Boiling point changes gradually along a series. Pentane sits between butane and hexane.
pool.explain: Pentane must boil between −1 °C and 69 °C; it boils at 36 °C. The trend is gradual, so the middle member lands in between.

pool.prompt: Mia says CH₃OH and C₃H₇OH cannot be in the same series because they are not next to each other. What is wrong?
choices: They differ by 2 × CH₂ and both have –OH, so they are in the same series
They have different numbers of oxygen atoms
pool.hint: A series is a whole family, not just a pair of neighbours.
pool.explain: Methanol and propanol are both alcohols. They differ by C₂H₄, which is two CH₂ steps, so they sit two places apart in one series.

pool.prompt: An alcohol has {n} carbon atoms. Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, how many hydrogen atoms does one molecule contain in total?
pool.hint: Count the hydrogens on the carbon chain, then remember the H in the –OH group.
pool.explain: 2 × {n} + 1 = {=2*n+1} H on the carbons, plus 1 in –OH, gives {=2*n+2} hydrogen atoms.

pool.prompt: The alkenes fit CₙH₂ₙ. How many hydrogen atoms are in the alkene with {n} carbon atoms?
pool.hint: Put n = {n} into CₙH₂ₙ: the H count is twice the C count.

pool.prompt: Why do all the alcohols react with sodium in a similar way?
choices: They all have the same functional group, –OH
They all have the same boiling point
They all have exactly two carbon atoms
pool.hint: The part of the molecule that reacts is the same in every member.
pool.explain: Every alcohol carries –OH, and that group does the reacting, so the reactions are similar even though chain lengths differ.

pool.prompt: Which pair is NOT in the same homologous series?
pool.hint: Same carbons does not mean same family. Check the general formula of each.
pool.explain: C₂H₄ is an alkene (CₙH₂ₙ) and C₂H₆ is an alkane (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂). The other pairs share a formula and differ by CH₂ steps.

visual.caption: Same series as ethanol, C₂H₅OH, or not? Look for the –OH group, not the carbon count. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: open the CH₂ gaps, test each family rule, sort by functional group, then guess boiling points.
